items.summary: The home page names the primary service in plain language.
The home page names the city served.
The home page opens with the problem and the outcome.
A primary action is visible on the home page.
Services are in the main navigation.
A service-area page exists for the sample city.
The same phone digits appear in the header, footer, and contact page.
The header phone is a click-to-call link.
The contact page has a form that posts to the site.
The form asks for no more than six required fields. Full scorecard points prefer five or fewer; the ZIP field is kept on purpose.
Form controls have labels and the expected input types.
Home, service, about, and contact pages each offer a next step.
The contact page states when someone calls back.
The contact page shows business hours.
The thank-you page says what happens next.
The form collects the service, the area, a message, and a preferred time.
A license slot is on the page and stays empty until a real number is added.
A guarantee slot is on the page and stays empty until a real term is added.
Pages set a device-width viewport.
Pages include a skip link and a mobile viewport.
Focus styles and 44px targets ship in the stylesheet.
Home, service, and location titles, descriptions, and H1s combine a service word with the city.
The home page is indexable and canonical. The 404 and thank-you pages are noindex. The sitemap lists public URLs.
Local business schema matches the visible name, phone, and street.
The service page and the location page are different documents.
An analytics snippet is injected only when a real GA4 or GTM id is set. Empty ids are not a failure.
